4.2.1 Scenic and Esthetic Resources
Plans for the restoration and enhancement of project lands during construction are presented in the Applicant's Exhibit W and Exhibit V, and in general state the following:
All practical means would be used to reduce adverse impacts on the surrounding environs. The primary areas of concern are reservoir clearing, borrow and spoil areas, construction yards and staging areas, access to the project, outlet works, and access tunnel adits. Access to the project would be by a road routed around the north side of the reservoir in order to minimize the visual effects on the Howard Creek area.
The supplemental borrow area contains approximately 2 million cubic yards of material; however, the Applicant does not plan to use this material unless suitable materials from primary borrow areas become exhausted. Borrow areas would be developed in an orderly manner, starting within the reservoir and woking outward to the borrow area limits. Borrow areas would be cleared and stripped of all undesirable material as they are developed. Those areas to be inundated would be sloped and terraced to minimize runoff and silting of streams. Borrow areas not inundated would be sloped and terraced to minimize runoff and silting of streams, and would be seeded with grass and legumes and reforested before construction of the project is completed. The limits of borrow areas have been set with due regard to the location of South Carolina Highway 171, thus leaving a strip of undisturbed forest between the highway and the borrow areas.
The area within the reservoir, as well as the embankment foundations, would be cleared and grubbed and all vegetation and stumps would be removed. Clearing would stop at elevation 2,315 feet, outside of the proposed borrow areas, 5 feet above the full pond elevation. Disturbed areas at the downstream face of embankments would be seeded with grass and legumes as soon as such work would not interfere with construction. Reforestation of these areas would take place before the construction of the project is completed.
